source_review.notes: Checked the Open Logic Project treatment of propositional and first-order semantics; Huth and Ryan, Enderton, Hoare, Dijkstra, Gries and Jackson for logic and specification foundations; and current Lean 4, SMT-LIB and Lamport specification references. Product/tool claims are qualified by selected logic, encoding, bounds and trusted base.

evidence: Checked the recursive propositional grammar and valuation semantics for negation, conjunction, disjunction, implication and biconditional.
Checked first-order signature, structure, assignment, satisfaction, free-variable and capture-avoiding substitution notation.
Checked state, input, final-state, result, execution relation, precondition, postcondition, invariant and refinement notation for consistent scopes and types.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Syntax, semantics, proof-system and execution-relation symbols are kept distinct; quantifier domains and assumptions are stated where material.

evidence: Recomputed all four Boolean valuations for material implication and negated-antecedent disjunction; each pair agrees and countermodel count is zero.
Recomputed maximum example for [1,2]: 3 satisfies the incomplete upper-bound clause but fails membership, while 2 satisfies both clauses.

Recomputed withdrawal boundary cases: sufficient balance permits the specified decrement on success; insufficient balance needs a separate failure obligation; failure preserves balance under the stated postcondition.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Numerical evidence is confined to finite Boolean enumeration and explicitly stated mathematical-integer examples.

evidence: Derived p implies q as not(p and not q) and as not p or q; checked equivalence over the complete two-atom valuation space.
Derived negations of universal and existential formulas and the tenant/server quantifier-order distinction.
Recomputed capture-avoiding substitution by alpha-renaming forall y.R(x,y) before replacing x with y.
Checked that partial-correctness, invariant initialization/preservation/exit and refinement obligations use the stated execution and observation relations.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Semantic entailment, syntactic provability, logical equivalence and empirical execution are not conflated.

evidence: Reviewed false antecedents, vacuous universal statements, empty collections, nonempty first-order domains and satisfiable but unreachable countermodels.
Reviewed machine overflow, floating-point NaN and signed zero, division by zero, partial maps, time discontinuity, solver unknown/timeout and finite exploration bounds.
Reviewed nondeterminism, divergence, frame conditions, errors, side effects, concurrency, fairness, environment assumptions and implementation/model correspondence.
Reviewed high-stakes medical-dose and autonomous train-door transfers, each requiring named domain, safety, security, regulatory and operational human review.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: The chapter separates modeled mathematical conclusions from deployment claims and gives explicit residual-risk boundaries.

evidence: Traced syntax/interpretation, domain/sort, variable scope, arithmetic, time, failure, nondeterminism, termination and observation assumptions through exposition, examples and answers.
Checked loop proof decomposition into initialization, preservation, exit and separate termination obligations.
Checked result specifications pair ordering or bound properties with membership/permutation and frame requirements so degenerate implementations are excluded.
invariant_checking.notes: Every invariant claim is relative to a defined transition or execution relation; reachability and inductiveness are explicitly distinguished.

evidence: Reviewed the four-case exhaustive proof of p implies q iff not p or q under classical two-valued semantics.
Checked disjunctive-syllogism countermodel argument and implication/contrapositive/converse classifications.
Checked quantified negation derivations, contract obligation quantifiers and the distinction between partial and total correctness.
Confirmed bounded model absence, testing success and solver results are not presented as universal program-correctness proofs.
proof_review.notes: Proof conclusions are explicitly conditional on formal definitions, axioms, encoding correctness, tool trust and implementation correspondence.

evidence: Audited uses of proves, valid, exhaustive, equivalent, entails, correct, safe and verified against the surrounding scope.
Separated truth-table proof, local proof obligations, bounded checking, property-test sampling, SMT results and interactive proof.
Confirmed medical and railway examples demand human review and do not claim external approval.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Finite and conditional arguments are labeled with their logic, state/domain bound or assumptions rather than promoted to universal deployment claims.

evidence: artifacts/snippets/TPROG-001/report.json
Reproduced four deterministic Boolean rows with equivalent=yes and countermodels=0 under recorded Python 3 toolchain evidence.
Confirmed the run excludes first-order quantification, nonclassical logics, temporal behavior, source-requirement translation, implementation execution and solver correctness.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Execution is evidence for one finite encoded equivalence only; the independent expression routes reduce circularity but do not validate arbitrary encodings.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter builds a coherent progression from propositional syntax and model theory through predicates, quantifiers, contracts, invariants, proof obligations and refinement without collapsing formal truth into real-world correctness.

practitioner_review.notes: Guidance covers ambiguous requirement translation, countermodel search, complete result and failure specifications, machine semantics, solver/tool evidence, implementation correspondence, traceability and high-stakes review boundaries.

pedagogical_review.notes: Objectives align with ten distinct worked examples and five exercises that progress from valuation and implication mechanics through quantified specifications, evidence selection and an unfamiliar safety-critical transfer problem.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
